newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia to buy Jefferson Bank for $542 million.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia to buy Jefferson Bank for $542 million.

text.p: North Carolina bank Wachovia Corp. announced plans Tuesday to buy Jefferson Bankshares Inc. for $542 million, ending a six-year hiatus from big bank acquisitions.
The friendly transaction, which values Jefferson at $38.83 a share, will significantly expand Wachovia's presence in the growing Virginia market.
The deal will also expand a 20-year relationship between the two banks and will reunite Jefferson Chief Executive Kenton McCartney, who left Wachovia in 1984, with his former employer.

"For some time we have been looking at strategic opportunities in attractive markets. Jefferson National is a very strong, well-managed bank located in a number of vibrant Virginia markets," Wachovia Chief Executive Leslie Baker said in a statement. Jefferson Bankshares, based in Charlottesville, Va., operates as Jefferson National.
Under the agreement, 0.625 share of Wachovia common stock will be exchanged for each Jefferson Bankshares share. The deal is structured to be tax-free to shareholders.
"It's a very attractive deal for Wachovia and everyone else concerned," said industry analyst John Mason at Interstate/Johnson Lane.

Wachovia, which had kept to the sidelines in the banking merger frenzy, recently expressed interest in expanding into Virginia. Its last sizeable acquisition came in 1991 when it bought South Carolina National.
Wachovia also indicated that it may not wait another six years for another big acquisition.

"We are very interested in growing our presence in the Southeast. You can look for us to be examining other specific markets in the months and years ahead," Baker said in a conference call with reporters, noting Maryland was a particularly attractive area.
Jefferson stock surged $7.75 to close at $37.75 on Nasdaq. Wachovia added 12.5 cents to $62.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the deal was expected to proceed smoothly and estimated it would be completed before the Oct. 31 target date given by the two companies. The deal is subject to approval of Jefferson shareholders and regulators. It has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies.
"It fits into (Wachovia's) strategy of expanding into high-growth markets in the Southeast," said Cheryl Swaim of Oppenheimer & Co.
Wachovia, based in Winston-Salem, N.C., has an option to acquire about 19.9 percent of Jefferson's outstanding shares if the deal does not close under certain circumstances.
The merger is expected to have a positive impact on Wachovia's earnings in 1998, it said.

Baker said Wachovia expects $18 million in annual cost savings from the transaction. Chief Financial Officer Robert McCoy said the company will take a $19 million charge against earnings for the acquisition, but timing of the charge has not yet been determined.

McCartney said he approached Baker about a transaction two weeks ago after an intensive study by the Jefferson board. Under the plan, McCartney will continue to run the Virginia operations after the merger.
"The companies are very similar from a cultural standpoint," said Darren Short of Robinson-Humphrey, who described Jefferson as "a miniature Wachovia" with a "penchant for conservatism".
